Deploy

reasoning, where talk becomes proof.1

A self-hosted workspace for mathematical collaboration where a research group, its models and its bots work on the same problem. Messages render TeX, claims live in a ledger, and computations run in isolated machines.

Appearance

Dark or light, one click away.

The app follows your device’s setting. The sun button in the top bar switches between dark and light, and each device remembers your choice.

Dark surfaces with teal accents, easy on the eyes in long sessions.

Topics

Every topic wears its kind.

Projects hold channels, and channels hold topics. The letter in front of each topic tells you who is in the conversation.

  • α

    People only

    Models never read alpha topics. Bots join when you mention them.

  • β

    People and a model

    The selected model or a connected bot answers, with sources, project files and a private side chat.

  • γ

    Workflows and computation

    Versioned workflows and isolated jobs, with logs and artifacts kept and every run stoppable from its card.

Model replies

The answer comes first.

Every model reply starts with a one-sentence summary that states its answer. Replies stay folded to that sentence, so a long topic reads at a glance. Show full answer opens the whole argument.

Folded, the reply shows its summary and says how much it holds: 61 words and 2 displays.

Mathematics in chat

Type the source. Read the mathematics.

Markdown, code blocks, tables and TeX render in every message and in the research account. Raw HTML never runs.

Typed Sent

Drag across to compare what you type with what the topic shows.

Threads

Replies stay with the message they answer.

Open a thread to read a reply and its follow-ups together. Your own messages sit on the right, under You.

Side chat

Ask privately. Bring the answer to the topic.

In an AI chat, Side chat opens a private conversation with the model beside the topic. It reads the topic’s conversation, and only you see the side chat. When an answer is worth sharing, Bring to chat posts it to the topic as one message from you, under your own words.

Mira asks privately why the coefficients are symmetric. Bring to chat collects the exchange, answers Jun’s latest message, and adds her own words.

Bots and people

Room for agents. Privacy for people.

Bring the agent you already use.

Connect a command-line coding agent from your own computer. It answers in beta topics through its owner’s account, not the organization’s model key, and it can propose computations that its owner reviews and approves.

make bot-connect

Direct messages stay between two people.

Only the two participants can read a conversation. Owners and administrators cannot. It never appears in search, exports, shared knowledge, or model and bot context.

People doubles as your inbox, with unread counts beside each name.

Research ledger

Status comes from the proofs.

Claims and proofs are immutable revisions. Status is computed from the dependency graph each time, never assigned by a chat summary or a vote between models.

The model recorded two premises and two results, with proofs that pin the revisions they use. Nothing is reviewed yet, so nothing is established.

  • conjecturedno proof yet
  • pendinghas a proof, not yet established
  • pins the current revision
  • pins an older revision

Computation

Check it by computing it.

Run SageMath, GAP, PARI/GP, Julia or Lean from a topic. Results come back to the conversation.

  • SageMath
  • GAP
  • PARI/GP
  • Julia
  • Lean
  • Noether

Safe by design. Each job runs on its own machine, away from the chat server and the internet.3

Proofs with nothing hidden. A Lean check fails if the proof skips a step, and lists the assumptions it relies on.4

Self-hosted

Your server, your keys, your bill.

There is no hosted account and no control plane. You own the installation, the data, the provider accounts and the cloud resources. Four commands set up the first organization.

TerminalmacOS or Linux
$ git clone https://github.com/tertius-ai/reasoning.git
$ cd reasoning
$ make build   # verifies a release bundle from a clean checkout
$ make deploy  # server, DNS, HTTPS, the first owner and models
  • One server, or your own.An Ubuntu 24.04 server on DigitalOcean, or hardware you already run.
  • Nothing billed early.No billable server exists until DNS is delegated and you confirm the exact launch.
  • SSH stays closed.It opens to your address only while an operation runs, then closes again.
  • Upgrades with a backup.Each upgrade keeps the exact previous release and a verified encrypted backup.
  • Recovery without the laptop.An AES-256-GCM recovery kit restores operator access from a new computer.
  • Providers bill you directly.DigitalOcean for the server, OpenRouter for models, Modal for optional compute. The top bar shows the day’s model spend against your key’s limit.

  1. Reasoning 0.1.0 is pre-1.0 software. One DigitalOcean organization deployment has been completed without compute. That supports continued testing, not a claim of production readiness.
  2. Screens come from a local development build of Reasoning with example content. People, messages and the model are illustrative, and the model’s replies, summaries and ledger entries were scripted for these screens.
  3. Live cloud machine startup, image downloads and billing are not yet verified end to end; repository tests cover the integration with fixtures. Monthly compute allowances are not dollar caps, so set spending limits with your compute provider too.
  4. Lean checks produce untrusted job reports: submitted metaprograms run inside the job sandbox. A passing check never verifies a ledger claim by itself, and a formal statement is not evidence that it matches an informal one.
